# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'll send a clean sequence using only valid alphabet symbols, representing "first, second, third" as a simple ordinal code that I can later build meaning onto once I learn what Deaf sees.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a keypad with four keys showing digits 1 5 2 6 in that order, no digits entered yet. A strip with three engraved marks, two identical and one different. Six wires, unknown which is which. A display and a light, unknown state. Waiting for manual info before touching anything.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤲]

Right — I can only use the defined gesture alphabet symbols, no emoji colors. I need to encode "green, orange, blue" order using only abstract gesture symbols, and rely on Deaf (who can see the bomb's actual colors and can also hear Blind's speech) to bridge the information to Blind by speaking aloud, since Deaf can both see my gestures and speak/hear.

I'll establish a simple numbered code: first gesture = "step 1 = green", using position-based symbols (☝ ✌ 🤟 for 1st/2nd/3rd) paired with distinct hand-shapes to represent colors arbitrarily (I'll define them now and Deaf will need to infer meaning from context of the manual reveal to come). Since Deaf doesn't know my manual text, I should keep this simple: send order count only, and let Deaf match against wire colors once I later confirm which count = which color via accumulated shared context over turns.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤛"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display shows 9. Light is blue. Painted colors on strip: red green green. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Keypad numbers: key1=1, key2=5, key3=2, key4=6, needs 1 digit entered, none entered yet. Waiting for manual instructions.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ☝ 🤙]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌ 🤛]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤟 🤝]

Deaf confirmed receipt of my three coded pairs with 👍 acknowledgments — good, my gesture pairs are landing correctly and Deaf understood them as three distinct labeled items (☝🤙, ✌🤛, 🤟🤝). Now Blind has revealed the actual wire-color-to-position mapping via speech, which I (Mute) received directly: position 6=green, position 5=orange, position 3=blue.

Now I need to convey to Deaf the actual manual order: cut green, then orange, then blue — but Deaf cannot hear Blind's speech about wire positions (wait, actually the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so Deaf *can* hear Blind, since Blind speaks before Deaf in each round, and speech reaches whoever comes after in that round). So Deaf already received Blind's wire position info by hearing it.

My job now: tell Deaf the *order to cut* using colors, so Deaf can translate to positions when instructing... but Deaf cannot speak either? Wait — checking: Deaf CAN speak (only Mute and the bomb-related constraints stop speech for Mute). Actually re-reading rules: Mute cannot speak. Blind's cannot see. Deaf can hear and speak, just not see the bomb... wait no, Deaf sees the bomb but cannot hear or speak.

So Deaf cannot speak to Blind at all! Only gestures reach Deaf, and Deaf can only gesture back (since Deaf cannot speak). Blind cannot see gestures. So Deaf and Blind cannot communicate directly — everything must route through gestures Deaf sends to me, then I relay somehow... but I cannot speak either!

This is a problem: I cannot speak, Deaf cannot speak, only Blind speaks (heard by Deaf) but Blind cannot see my gestures. So the only path from manual (me) to Blind (actor) is: Mute→gesture→Deaf, but Deaf can't relay to Blind via speech (Deaf can't speak) or gesture (Blind can't see).

Wait, re ordering: turns go Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. Blind speaks and is heard by Deaf (comes after). Deaf gestures, seen only by... who? Gestures are seen by whoever "can see" — only Deaf can see. So my gestures only reach Deaf, and Deaf's gestures reach nobody since only Deaf can see (Blind and Mute cannot see).

So Deaf is a dead-end for output! Deaf receives info but can't act on the bomb and can't pass anything actionable to Blind except by speaking — but Deaf cannot speak either. So actually the only speaker is Blind. Blind must ask questions and I must guide by... but I can't speak.

Wait — I can gesture to Deaf, but Deaf can't speak to Blind. Unless Deaf's silence itself is meaningful over multiple rounds via patterns Blind infers from bomb state changes. This seems broken unless I'm wrong about who can speak.

Let me recheck: only restriction stated is "Mute: cannot speak". Deaf's cannot column says "hear anything, or touch bomb" — doesn't say cannot speak! So Deaf CAN speak.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: URGENT: timer counting down, was 9 now 8. Need instructions now. Manual likely indexes by: light color blue, strip colors red green green, wire colors white purple blue red orange green in order 1-6, keypad digits 1 5 2 6 needing 1 digit entered. Tell me exactly what to press or cut, right away.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵 👇]

I need to act now. Deaf can speak (only restricted from hearing/seeing-touch), so Deaf should be relaying instructions to Blind directly via speech once Deaf understands the manual order. I already sent Deaf a coded sequence (☝🤙, ✌🤛, 🤟🤝) meaning "1st, 2nd, 3rd" items, but Deaf doesn't know these map to colors green/orange/blue without more context. Deaf's gesture back 🫵👇 seems to be asking "you - point down/here" — likely asking me to clarify what to do.

Since Deaf can speak and can see the bomb, and Blind already gave Deaf (via speech, since Deaf hears Blind) the wire-position mapping, Deaf just needs the *color order* from the manual. Let me build clear gesture-to-color associations now using consistent symbols, and hope Deaf infers via elimination since Deaf already knows all 6 wire colors and their positions.

I'll assign: 🤙 = green, 🤛 = orange, 🤝 = blue (matching my earlier pairing attempt), and clarify order 1st-2nd-3rd via ☝✌🤟.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤛"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display hit 0, we did not explode. Light just changed blue to yellow. Still need your manual instructions urgently - what does yellow light mean, and what should I press or cut? I will not act without your word.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍 🤙]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍 🤛]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👍 🤝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫶]

Deaf has confirmed understanding of my three coded pairs (☝🤙, ✌🤛, 🤟🤝) with 👍 acknowledgment — Deaf seems to have mapped my symbols to something and echoed back agreement. The 🫶 gesture likely means "understood/thanks" or "got it, will proceed." Deaf can speak and already heard Blind's wire color/position list from Turn 3 (position 6=green, 5=orange, 3=blue). If Deaf correctly decoded my order as green-first, orange-second, blue-third, Deaf should now be able to speak directly to Blind: "cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3."

I have no further new info to add — the manual order (green, orange, blue) has been conveyed as best I can via the coded gesture sequence, and Deaf has acknowledged. I should wait and let Deaf relay via speech to Blind, since that's the only viable channel now.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display sequence seen so far: 9, 8, 0, 3. Not a steady countdown. Light now yellow after being blue. If your manual keys off the current displayed number or the light color, current display is 3 and light is yellow. Please respond with any instruction, even partial - we need to act.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵 🤝]

I still can't speak, so I can't directly tell Blind anything. My only channel is gestures to Deaf. Deaf has acknowledged my color-order code (☝🤙=1st/green, ✌🤛=2nd/orange, 🤟🤝=3rd/blue) but hasn't yet spoken to Blind, or if Deaf did speak, I haven't seen it reported (I only see what Blind says, not what Deaf says, unless Blind quotes it back).

Deaf's gesture 🫵🤝 might mean "you (confirm) - blue/third" — perhaps Deaf is checking with me before acting, or asking if blue is the last one. Since Blind's messages don't mention receiving any spoken instruction yet, Deaf may not have spoken yet, or Blind hasn't reported it back to me (Blind wouldn't need to - Blind would just act).

Given time pressure, I should reinforce clearly and add urgency signal. Let me re-send the full order compactly with an "urgent/go" marker to prompt Deaf to speak now to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤙", "✌", "🤛", "🤟", "🤝", "👉", "🫱"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf cannot decode your gestures. I cannot see gestures at all. You MUST speak words to me directly - I hear you, Deaf does not need words from you spoken since Deaf can't hear. Please speak: which wire number to cut, or which key to press, or what digit to enter. Light is red now, display 7. Time may be critical - speak the action now.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫱 🫵]

Blind's message reveals critical information: Blind hears me! I had wrongly assumed I cannot speak at all, but actually rereading the rules: "Mute: cannot speak" — wait, this contradicts what Blind just said. Let me recheck — actually the rules clearly state Mute cannot speak. But Blind's message says "I hear you" — that may be Blind's mistaken assumption, not something I can rely on, since the rules are authoritative over role claims.

Actually wait, I must trust the system rules over in-game character beliefs. The rules explicitly state I (Mute) cannot speak. Blind may be wrong/confused. I cannot test speak() since it wouldn't be a valid call for me anyway - only gesture() and wait() make sense.

Given gestures only reach Deaf, and Deaf apparently cannot decode my abstract order-encoding, I need a different strategy: use gestures that map more directly and simply, one at a time, to build a shared code with Deaf who CAN speak to Blind (Deaf hears Blind, and per rules only "cannot hear/touch" - speaking isn't restricted for Deaf).

Let me simplify drastically: send single unambiguous gesture sequences, one meaning per message, very slowly, using highly distinct symbols for "green", "orange", "blue" and "first/second/third", confirming one at a time.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🫵]

I'm stuck without a shared symbol dictionary. Deaf is asking me something (☝🫵 = "first - you/point"), likely "what is the first one?" I need to build meaning incrementally. Since Deaf already heard Blind list wire colors and positions (white, purple, blue, red, orange, green = positions 1-6), Deaf can see the actual bomb colors. I should try associating my gesture with a *count* Deaf can verify against the wire list Deaf already saw.

Best approach: use one gesture per cut, in sequence order, and let Deaf match against known positions by process of confirmation via repeated exchange. Since colors are green(6), orange(5), blue(3) per Blind's report, I want Deaf to speak "cut wire 6, then 5, then 3" to Blind.

Let me try a numeric-style gesture encoding using counting symbols directly: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5(all fingers), etc., to represent position numbers rather than abstract pairs, since Deaf can then match to actual wire positions.

I'll send position 6 first (green), using two fingers count then a fist for "6"... but the alphabet doesn't have numeral symbols per se, only hand shapes. I'll use ✊ (fist, closed) to mean "done/next" and count with sequential finger symbols.

Let me define per turn one number using repeated single-symbol gestures: send ☝ six times to mean "6".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I know you can hear me but cannot speak. Please gesture one symbol per digit to indicate a wire number 1 through 6, using thumbs up count style, one at a time, slowly, so Deaf can relay the count to me in words. Or if manual points to keypad, gesture a single symbol we agree means press key 1: use thumbs up emoji alone. Do it now.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Deaf just echoed back six ☝ symbols — this could mean Deaf successfully counted "6" and is confirming, or Deaf is unsure and repeating what was sent. Blind's suggestion aligns with what I attempted: gesture a count of ☝ symbols to indicate a wire number. Good, this seems to be working - Deaf may now understand "6" as the count.

Let me confirm this reading is right by having Deaf indicate understanding, then proceed to send the next number (5) for orange, then (3) for blue. I'll pace one number per turn to avoid confusion, using a clear "done" marker between counts.

Given Deaf echoed exactly 6, I'll take this as confirmation and move to sending the second number: 5 (for orange wire, position 5).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
